country_background: Australia, a constitutional monarchy with its capital in Canberra, had 27.9 million residents at 31 March 2026.{{country_overview.demographics:1}}{{country_overview.demographics:3}} The King is head of state, represented by Governor-General Sam Mostyn.{{country_overview.government:1}} Labor won 94 seats at the 2025 federal election, and Anthony Albanese continues as Prime Minister, with Mark Butler as Minister for Health and Ageing.{{country_overview.government:3}}{{country_overview.government:4}}{{country_overview.government:5}} GDP was about US$1.80 trillion in 2025, but consumer prices rose 4.3 percent in the 12 months to September 2026 and unemployment was 4.7 percent.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:7}}{{country_overview.economy:8}} Life expectancy is 81.1 years for men and 85.1 for women, and 17.7 percent of residents are 65 or older.{{country_overview.demographics:9}}{{country_overview.demographics:4}} The key risk is access: only 53.4 percent of emergency stays ended within four hours in 2024-25.{{health_system.hospitals:1}}
key_takeaways: Health spending was 10.5 percent of GDP in 2024-25 on the AIHW basis, and governments funded 70 percent.{{health_system.financing:1}}{{health_system.financing:2}}
GP bulk billing reached 83.6 percent of services in July to September 2026, against 77.6 percent a year earlier.{{health_system.public_system:6}}
Specialists bill differently: 28.1 percent of attendances were bulk billed in July to September 2025.{{health_system.public_system:8}}
Under the OECD estimate, spending was 10.84 percent of GDP in 2024, above the OECD mean of 9.30 percent.{{health_system.financing:3}}
health_system: Medicare is universal public insurance, and the states and territories run public hospitals.{{health_system.public_system:1}}
The 2026 original Medicare safety net is A$594.40 (US$417), and the extended net for general patients is A$2,699.10 (US$1,890).{{health_system.public_system:12}}
Nurse density is 13.42 per 1,000 people, above the OECD mean of 9.93.{{health_system.workforce:2}}
market: At 30 June 2026, 12,823,752 people, or 45.8 percent of the population, held hospital cover.{{health_system.private_system:1}}
Medibank including ahm holds 26.5 percent and Bupa 25.5 percent of insurance, per CHOICE's summary of APRA data.{{health_system.private_system:2}}
Healthscope's 25 hospitals are going to four operators, but Calvary said the 30 November handover would be delayed.{{health_system.hospitals:9}}{{health_system.hospitals:10}}
risks: Premiums rose 4.41 percent on average on 1 April 2026, the largest increase since 2017.{{health_system.private_system:3}}
APHA, citing ABS data, puts the private hospital sector's 2024-25 operating loss at A$756 million (US$530 million).{{health_system.hospitals:3}}
Over 3,000 older patients were waiting in public beds for aged care places.{{health_system.hospitals:12}}

recent.text: ABS data show dementia caused 10.1 percent of deaths in 2025, the first year above 10 percent.{{recent_developments.1:1}}
Receivers announced the Healthscope sale to Calvary, Healthe Care, ACURIO Health and KnG Group, with the ACCC yet to decide.{{recent_developments.2:1}}{{recent_developments.2:3}}
The 2026-27 Budget gives the states A$220.3 billion (US$154 billion) over five years for public hospitals.{{recent_developments.3:1}}
